title: Rome: an overseas republic
hook: When did Rome’s reach become more than Italian?

knows: Events happen in places and at different times.

objective: Rome’s expansion crossed water as well as land.

claims.text: 272 BCE: Italy. Rome’s expansion reaches southern Italy.
claims.source: https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/6-4-the-roman-republic — Italy map, Punic Wars and Macedonian wars

claims.text: 241 BCE: Sicily. The First Punic War brings Sicily.
claims.source: https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/6-4-the-roman-republic — Italy map, Punic Wars and Macedonian wars

claims.text: 201 BCE: Iberia. Rome acquires Carthaginian territory in Iberia.
claims.source: https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/6-4-the-roman-republic — Italy map, Punic Wars and Macedonian wars

claims.text: 146 BCE: Across the sea. Roman armies destroy Carthage and Corinth.
claims.source: https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/6-4-the-roman-republic — Italy map, Punic Wars and Macedonian wars

claims.text: Rome’s expansion crossed water as well as land. Sicily became an overseas possession after the First Punic War; subsequent wars brought Iberian territory and interventions farther east. These selected events show a changing Mediterranean reach, not a uniform block of Roman control.
claims.source: https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/6-4-the-roman-republic — Italy map, Punic Wars and Macedonian wars

claims.text: Connections mark selected events; no territorial boundaries or full conquest chronology.
